task.description: REVIEWER hard gate (WF-02 Step 2d) on REQ-163's decision artefact -- no code exists for this requirement, so this gate's focus is decision-record consistency and scope-creep, not OTP idiom. CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR already independently re-verified the cited wasmex web evidence and passed. Your job: confirm this artefact does not silently reopen or contradict decision 0014's own settled premises (wasmex adoption, process-boundary mandate), confirm the artefact's own placement decision (lib/letflow/design/ vs. a new docs/migration/decisions/ record) is consistent with how this project has handled similar scoping calls before (cite the REQ-150/OQ-6 precedent it claims to mirror and verify that precedent is real), and confirm no scope creep -- this requirement's own text is explicit that NO mix.exs change and NO lib/letflow/engine/ file may be touched.
acceptance_criteria: Confirm the artefact does not silently reopen or contradict any of decision 0014's settled premises -- read 0014 in full and check for contradiction, not just citation.

Confirm the REQ-150/OQ-6 placement precedent the artefact cites is real -- read lib/letflow/design/req150-lua-number-marshalling.md's own framing/placement rationale and confirm it is genuinely analogous.

Confirm no scope creep: git diff --stat main...feature/WF02-REQ163-20260828 touches only this run's own handoffs/, docs/status/, handoffs/registry.json bookkeeping, and lib/letflow/design/req163-wasm-abi-choice.md -- no mix.exs, no lib/letflow/engine/ file.
Confirm the artefact's open questions (section 6) are genuinely deferred rather than silently resolved by assumption.

Confirm the artefact does not overstate its own authority -- it explicitly should not claim to bind REQ-166/167/171/172 beyond what a design-level (not decision-record-level) artefact can bind, while still being concrete enough to prevent those future requirements from re-deriving the same research.
CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field (line 9) must be exactly PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish -- run mix letflow.lint_handoffs before finishing.

findings: No contradiction with decision 0014: read 0014 in full. REQ-163 only settles OQ-4 (core modules vs. component model), which 0014 explicitly leaves open and instructs S5 to 'pick one explicitly.' Wasmex adoption and the mandatory process-boundary (0014 Decision (2), Reasoning (a)) are cited, not touched -- section 3.3 explicitly defers dispatch mechanics to PluginInterface.invoke/2,3's existing process-boundary pattern rather than redesigning it.

REQ-150/OQ-6 precedent verified as real and analogous: lib/letflow/design/req150-lua-number-marshalling.md is itself a design-only artefact (not a decisions/ record) resolving OQ-6 for the identical structural reason REQ-163 claims -- it operates entirely inside 0014's premise (adopting tv-labs/lua) rather than revising it, and section 4 of that doc explicitly hands off a WASM-side parity obligation to REQ-171/REQ-172, the same forward-reference pattern REQ-163 uses for REQ-166/167/171/172.

Scope confirmed via `git diff --stat main...feature/WF02-REQ163-20260828`: only handoffs/ bookkeeping (step-01, step-01b, step-02d) and lib/letflow/design/req163-wasm-abi-choice.md changed (4 files, 462 insertions, 0 deletions). No mix.exs, no lib/letflow/engine/ file touched.

Section 6's three open items (alloc export failure-mode contract, :i64 overflow structured-error shape, wasmex beta-status revisit trigger) are genuinely left to REQ-166/REQ-171/REQ-172 -- none is silently resolved by assumption elsewhere in the artefact; each is stated as a decision explicitly deferred, with the owning future requirement named.

Authority is appropriately scoped: the artefact justifies its own placement in lib/letflow/design/ (not a new decisions/ record) on the same narrow-premise test 0014 and REQ-150 already established, and its strong binding language toward REQ-166/167/171/172 ('the one ABI shape... implemented against') mirrors REQ-150 section 2's identical binding style for a design-level artefact -- consistent with how this project already treats design docs as prescriptive within their own stage, not an overreach into decision-record-level, cross-stage bindingness.

Worth watching, not blocking: sections 3.1-3.2 (the implicit `alloc` export requirement, the descriptor-pointer convention) and section 5 (the full numeric-mapping table) go somewhat beyond a minimal core-vs-component pick into concrete ABI design. This is consistent with the requirement's own stated scope ('blocks WASM-02/WASM-07's concrete ABI') and is not scope creep against mix.exs/engine code, but REQ-166 should treat these as REQ-163's contribution to consume, not re-litigate, rather than the two docs quietly diverging later.
